from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Guessing Game", [
            "Wordle is a game of uncertainty.",
            "We want to minimize our guesses.",
            "We do this by maximizing information gain."
        ])
        
        # Setup visual elements
        items = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.6, color=BLUE).add(Text(str(i+1), font_size=16)) for i in range(16)])
        items.arrange_in_grid(rows=4, cols=4, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(items, "B2", "E5")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(items))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Sequential search demo
        for item in items:
            self.play(item.animate.set_color(RED), run_time=0.1)
            self.play(item.animate.set_color(BLUE), run_time=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Binary reduction concept placeholder
        binary_hint = Text("Binary Reduction?", color=GREEN, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(binary_hint, "C3")
        self.play(FadeIn(binary_hint))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Measuring Uncertainty with Entropy", [
            "Entropy measures uncertainty in a system.",
            "It shows how information is distributed.",
            "Think of it as probability branches."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Entropy H(S) = - sum p(x) log2 p(x)
        entropy_formula = MathTex(r"H(S) = -\sum p(x) \log_2 p(x)", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(entropy_formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(entropy_formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualize entropy: pie chart-like structure (or nodes)
        chart = VGroup(
            Dot(color=BLUE),
            Dot(color=BLUE),
            Dot(color=BLUE)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(chart, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(chart))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Probability branches
        branches = VGroup(
            Line(ORIGIN, UP+RIGHT),
            Line(ORIGIN, UP+LEFT)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(branches, 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(branches))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Every guess splits possible words.",
            "Feedback categorizes remaining words.",
            "Choose words to split pools equally.",
            "Balanced buckets maximize information.",
            "Information gain reveals answer faster."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Logic: Information Gain", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Define Information Gain as reduction in entropy.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        entropy_text = Text("Gain(S, A) = H(S) - H(S|A)", font_size=24, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(entropy_text, "B2")
        self.play(Write(entropy_text))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Feedback categorizes remaining words.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        words_pool = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, color=GRAY, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(10)])
        words_pool.arrange_in_grid(2, 5)
        self.place_at_grid(words_pool, "D3")
        self.play(Create(words_pool))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Choose words to split pools equally.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        arrow = Arrow(self.grid["D3"], self.grid["E5"])
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Balanced buckets maximize information.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        bucket1 = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=1.0, color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["F2"])
        bucket2 = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=1.0, color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["F4"])
        self.play(Create(bucket1), Create(bucket2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Information gain reveals answer faster.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        check_mark = Tex(r"$\checkmark$", color=RED).scale(2).move_to(self.grid["E3"])
        self.play(Write(check_mark))
        self.wait(2)

            "Entropy transforms guessing into solving.",
            "Master architects systematically narrow choices."

        self.place_at_grid(gain_text, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)

outline.topic: Decoding Wordle: Using Information Theory to Win

sections.title: Introduction: The Guessing Game
sections.content: Introduce Wordle as a decision-making game under uncertainty. Define the goal: minimize the number of guesses by maximizing 'information gain' per turn.
sections.example: A 'Wordle-bot' (a cartoon owl) faces a 5-letter word puzzle. Instead of guessing randomly, it evaluates the 'surprise' value of its choices.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Measuring Uncertainty with Entropy
sections.content: Introduce Shannon Entropy (H). Explain it as the average amount of 'information' produced by a stochastic source. Visualize this as a 'Probability Tree' where branches represent possible word outcomes.
sections.example: Graphical chart: A pie chart showing the distribution of remaining possible words. Entropy is the measure of how 'flat' or 'spiky' this distribution is.

sections.title: The Core Logic: Information Gain
sections.content: Explain that every guess splits the remaining word pool into smaller subsets based on the color-coded feedback (Gray, Yellow, Green). The 'best' guess is the one that splits the pool into the most balanced groups, effectively maximizing the expected information gain.
sections.example: Animation showing a word like 'CRANE' splitting a set of 2,000 words into 50 distinct color-pattern buckets, versus a word like 'XYLYL' which leaves most words in one giant bucket.

sections.title: Application: The Strategy in Action
sections.content: Demonstrate the iterative process: 1. Calculate entropy for all valid words. 2. Pick the word with the highest score. 3. Update the candidate list based on feedback. 4. Repeat.
sections.example: A visual flow diagram where 'CRANE' (the input) filters a dictionary of 12,972 words down to a narrow list of 50, showing the entropy plummeting from high to low.

sections.title: Conclusion: Summary and Intuition
sections.content: Summarize that winning at Wordle isn't about vocabulary; it's about systematically reducing the 'state space' of unknown information. Final takeaway: Entropy is the tool to transform guessing into solving.
sections.example: Final slide: The cartoon owl transforming from a frustrated guesser into a 'Master Architect' who visualizes the game as a narrowing funnel of data.
